summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 10, part 34) set in a bookshop staffed and frequented by young people in a future setting with exoskeletons, games, and a curated book distributorship. The narrator Chloe sells four items to a buyer at a price discussed against a UCL student's offer, then sits behind the counter watching kids, noting her store's upward trend in young visitors. It is Arthur Levitt's 110th birthday, and he is due for an inspection tour; he founded the distributorship that places small selections of books in retailers that admit young people. Her store manager Marcel teases her about how long she has known Arthur, and about her past as author Chloe Autumn.
one_line: Chloe Autumn, an elderly author-bookseller in a future shop for young people, awaits the 110th birthday visit of Arthur Levitt, founder of the book distributorship.
key_facts: Chloe sets the price for four items at fifteen pounds each, suggesting the buyer sell them for thirty.
The UCL student's offer to the buyer was a 40 percent discount on items that were otherwise priced at forty pounds or more.
Chloe has been perched on a stool for seventy-some years before giving it up.
Chloe was fitted with an exoskeleton on her 90th birthday that locks into a seated position.
Kids in the shop are described as having flawless skin and teeth because no parent would dare choose otherwise at conception.
Chloe's graph of young people in the shop shows an upward trend over time.
It is Arthur's 110th birthday, and he is meant to make one of his rare tours of inspection of the shop.
Arthur Levitt started the distributorship that put small, carefully curated handfuls of books into the few retailers across the land who let young people in.
Marcel is Chloe's store manager and is only a few years older than the kids in the shop.
Marcel says the first time he met Arthur, he was riding a brontosaurus.
Chloe says she was fourteen, no fifteen, when she first met Arthur, before he was Sir Arthur Levitt, Savior of English Literacy.
Marcel teases Chloe about being Chloe Autumn, superstar author.
Chloe's writing had stopped mattering to readers decades before Marcel was born, according to the narration.
The shop's tea is described as Pu'er, Chinese, mostly.
